_: Draft cards. One pick per stage cleared, 3 offered. See docs/05-powers.md for the calibration method. `gain` is an ESTIMATED percentage of per-stage capability against the measured floor baseline (~158 pts/stage); these are the numbers the simulation must confirm, not numbers it has confirmed.
_calibration: Targets grow 25% per stage and the player gets exactly one pick per stage, so the average pick must be worth slightly LESS than 25% or the ladder becomes infinite. Target: commons 8-15%, uncommons 15-25%, rares 25-35%.
_measured: gain is a percentage of a floor player's per-stage capability, and docs/05 1 was always explicit that every one of these is an ESTIMATE to be confirmed by simulation. Eight now are confirmed, by test/sim/meta_sim.dart measureCard, and they carry "measured": true. The estimates were wrong by 2x to 8x in BOTH directions: fine_yarn 6 -> 16, slub_yarn 8 -> 29, standard_yarn 18 -> 48, selvage 14 -> 48, quick_shuttle 3 (as implemented) -> fixed, temple 2 -> fixed. Read the unflagged numbers as guesses, because that is what they are. Two caveats on the measured ones. (1) They are MARGINAL against a no-build baseline, which is how docs/05 1 defines gain - but they do NOT compose: eleven picks at these values would be astronomical, while 85% unlocks measurably wins only 20% of its runs. The three gates are the only trustworthy statement about the whole game. (2) The sim cannot price tools, bag cards or the draft-widening cards at all; see unmeasurableCards in meta_sim.dart. A 0% there is an absence of evidence, not a dead card.
_placementScoring: Placing a block scores NOTHING on its own as of 2026-11-12 - points come from clearing a row or a column, full stop. cellValueFor now starts at ZERO instead of 1, so placement scoring is bought or drafted band by band: the three shop yarns turn it on permanently for their size band, the yarn CARDS do it for a run, Slub Yarn for one motif you name, and TABBY for every band at once. Nothing in the family is dead without the others, which is why it is built this way rather than as one enabler card gating eight pieces of content - a first attempt made Tabby an enabler worth a measured +125%, and a single card that decides the run is the offer deciding the run. The gains on the yarn family were measured when placement scoring was unconditional; they now need re-measuring and are marked unmeasured again.
_regated: 2026-11-11. Four unlocks were firing on events rather than achievements, which is not what docs/05 4 means by 'paced to skill'. double_pick (a RARE at +26%) moved from 'clear 3 lines at once' - which can happen by luck on run 1 - to 'clear stage 7'. jacquard_card moved from 'own 8 motifs' to 'own 10', because six motifs are free at install now. patience dropped to gain 16 and stacks 1: base patience went 2 to 3, so the card reads 3->4 now, a smaller relative gain for the same printed text. steady_beat rose to gain 18 because the x4.00 cap is ALWAYS reached at 85% unlocks and above, so raising it is worth more than it was priced at. See docs/05 8.
_poolIsFixedAtRunStart: The draft reads the milestones the account had when the run BEGAN, not live (RunController._poolMilestones). Reading them live meant clearing stage 7 put Second Shuttle into the next draft of the run that earned it: measured, a 0%-unlock account was offered 24 distinct cards including three rares, so '0% unlocks' did not mean the initial twelve. A run's pool should be knowable at its start - the same argument docs/06 6 makes for faults. Milestones earned mid-run still bank; they take effect from the next run.

offer._weights: Rarity weights by stage cleared, as common/uncommon/rare.
